key_insight: Predictive triboelectric nanogenerator design requires linking evolving real contact area and contact-dependent charge generation and decay to electrical output across scales.
engineering_relevance: Coupling material selection, interface mechanics and circuit response can guide reliable mechanical-energy harvesting and self-powered sensing.
method: Review polymeric, inorganic, composite and natural materials against charge retention, compliance and durability requirements.
Assess modelling from molecular and first-principles calculations to contact mechanics, device electrostatics and equivalent circuits.
Organise applications by device scale and propose staged validation of contact mechanics, electrostatics and circuit response.
evidence_signal: The review assesses model inputs, predicted quantities and experimental validation evidence, and proposes independent testing beyond calibration conditions.
watch_item: Prescribed surface charge density, idealised geometries and nominal contact-area assumptions can limit predictions under realistic loading.
paper_title: Triboelectric nanogenerators across length scales: linking materials, multiscale modelling and applications
